content.title: About
content.content: All‑purpose wheat flour is an enriched, bleached product made from selected wheat varieties. It has a fine texture, neutral flavor, and is suitable for a wide range of culinary uses, including bread, cakes, cookies, and pizza dough.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enriched flour contains added B‑vitamins and iron to replace nutrients lost during processing.
Bleaching makes the flour whiter but does not alter its nutritional profile.
All‑purpose flour has a moderate protein (gluten) content, making it ideal for tender baked goods.
Wheat flour is one of the most consumed food products worldwide.
Many wheat varieties exist, but soft wheat is typically used for all‑purpose flour.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Flour is rich in carbohydrates that quickly convert to energy needed by the body.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Enriched flour supplies thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Added iron helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber aids regular bowel function.

items.title: Versatile culinary base
items.content: Flour serves as the foundation for baking, sauces, breading, and many traditional dishes.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or gluten intolerance, requiring avoidance of flour.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Flour can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Nutrient loss over time
items.content: Prolonged storage in poor conditions may reduce vitamin levels.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Flour can be used for baking bread, cakes, cookies, pancakes, coating meat or vegetables, and thickening sauces and soups. Sift before use to remove lumps if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent pests and oxidation of any residual fats.
